inspiration.observed_pattern: A duplicate-key update compares an incoming checkpoint with the current row and conditionally assigns several fields in one multi-column upsert.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one parcel row and one newer checkpoint so MariaDB's left-to-right duplicate-update assignment semantics are observable without the larger parcel ledger.

fixture_notes: The existing parcel checkpoint advances from 5 to 7, but MariaDB leaves later fields at their prior values because the first assignment changes the value used by subsequent guards.
determinism_notes: One fixed parcel row and one fixed checkpoint use literal identifiers, timestamps, and values; the final read is primary-key ordered and has no clocks or concurrency.
setup: CREATE TABLE parcel_state_min (parcel_id VARCHAR(16) PRIMARY KEY, checkpoint_seq INT NOT NULL, location_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, next_location_code VARCHAR(16) NULL, recorded_at DATETIME NOT NULL, state_kind VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO parcel_state_min (parcel_id, checkpoint_seq, location_code, next_location_code, recorded_at, state_kind) VALUES ('P-100', 7, 'HUB-B', 'HUB-C', '2025-03-01 10:00:00', 'in_transit') ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE checkpoint_seq = IF(VALUES(checkpoint_seq) > parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq, VALUES(checkpoint_seq), parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq), location_code = IF(VALUES(checkpoint_seq) > parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq, VALUES(location_code), parcel_state_min.location_code), next_location_code = IF(VALUES(checkpoint_seq) > parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq, VALUES(next_location_code), parcel_state_min.next_location_code), recorded_at = IF(VALUES(checkpoint_seq) > parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq, VALUES(recorded_at), parcel_state_min.recorded_at), state_kind = IF(VALUES(checkpoint_seq) > parcel_state_min.checkpoint_seq, VALUES(state_kind), parcel_state_min.state_kind)

checks.sql: SELECT parcel_id, checkpoint_seq, location_code, next_location_code, recorded_at, state_kind FROM parcel_state_min ORDER BY parcel_id
